cases.title: Agent Offline During Hub Script Update；恢复后幂等、持久化、Desired State与实际状态一致
cases.canonical_before: PARTIAL — remaining: 无单独注入 duplicate/lost/reordered 通知帧或调度幂等维度。

covered_dimensions.layer: real-api + frame-wire injection (drop / duplicate / stale replay) + owned child Agent SQLite + Hub read-only SQLite desired-state compare
description: Lost notification: the real CHANGE_NOTIFICATION for a Hub Script update (global revision 3473) was dropped on the child channel; the child still converged to the new revision/sha within 19.184s via its own revision-check path (no silent divergence).

Duplicate notification: the real CHANGE_NOTIFICATION for the next Script update (global revision 3474) was delivered twice; the child converged once and idempotently in 0.351s with a single script row.

Reordered/stale delivery: the captured older notification (global revision 3473, script revision 2) was replayed after the newer revision 3 had been applied; the child kept revision 3 and the newest sha, and its global revision never regressed — i.e. a stale/reordered notification is ignored.

Desired state vs actual state after the fault window: all 9 owned scripts (revision+sha256), 9 owned tasks and 7 owned schedules match the Hub, and the live agent-owned schedule still produced exactly one execution per slot (no duplicate slots in Hub or child journal).

Restart persistence: the owned Agent was really stopped and restarted; definitions survived, every pre-restart execution id is still present with no duplicate ids, and the only new rows are genuinely new slots.

remaining_or_limitations: On the shared repair authority the SYNC_REQUEST count inside the replay window is not a clean discriminator (heartbeat revision checks every 5s plus other batches' object changes); the applied-state comparison is the authoritative signal and is what the assertion uses.

cases.title: `allow_offline` 与 `hub_online_required` 组合。
cases.canonical_before: PARTIAL — remaining: 两策略组合下的实际投递行为未验证。

covered_dimensions.layer: real-schedule (agent-owned 30s interval) + real channel cut on the owned child + node status + child journal offline/synced flags + Hub rows after reconnect
description: Quadrant 1+2 (child connected): both the allow_offline and the hub_online_required schedule fired (2 rows each, offline flag 0).
Quadrant 3 (child channel cut, allow_offline): 3 executions were created while disconnected, all with offline=1 and synced=0 (local-only until reconnect).

Quadrant 4 (child channel cut, hub_online_required): exactly 0 executions — the online gate really suppresses dispatch while the child has no Hub connection (the cut stops the listener, so the agent can never complete a handshake).

Recovery: after the channel was restored the Hub itself had already marked the node offline (observed 2.005s after the cut) and then online/synced; the offline executions were uploaded and appear as Hub rows with offline=true (3 rows); the hub_online_required schedule compensated the 3 missed slots with exactly 1 catch-up execution and then resumed its normal cadence.
No duplicate slots and the marker files match the child journal row counts exactly (business effect oracle).

remaining_or_limitations: The cut was implemented as "close both relay legs + stop the proxy listener" on the child's own channel; the Hub-side node status transition to offline was observed in 2.0s.

cases.title: `run_once` 与 `skip` Misfire。
cases.canonical_before: PARTIAL — remaining: 漏触发真实场景（停机后补偿）未验证。

covered_dimensions.layer: real-schedule (agent-owned 30s interval) + real Agent process stop/restart + child journal slot semantics + Hub row after reconnect
description: The Agent process was really stopped (2026-10-16T09:35:04Z) across 3 missed 30s slots and really restarted (2026-10-16T09:36:41Z); the slot arithmetic is done in the child clock frame (measured offset -0.035s).

run_once schedule: exactly 1 compensation execution after the restart, reporting the missed slot 2026-10-16T09:36:29Z (inside the stopped window) while starting at 2026-10-16T09:36:40.157695626Z — i.e. one catch-up for 3 missed boundaries, not one execution per missed slot; then normal cadence resumed.
skip schedule: 0 catch-up executions for the same stop window (no slot older than the restart was ever executed) and normal cadence resumed at the next boundary (2 rows after the restart).
The run_once compensation is visible on the Hub as the same execution id / slot (UI reads the same rows) and both schedules keep one execution per slot with marker lines matching row counts.

remaining_or_limitations: Overlap note (per the authorization checklist): the one-time "missed slot" SKIP/RUN_ONCE evidence already exists in p-sched phase5/phase9 (E2E-06). This run adds the INTERVAL-schedule dimension plus a real process stop/restart, which was not covered before.
